correctness.rationale: The inverse candidate is uniquely \(y=\lfloor x/\alpha\rfloor+1\) for irrational \(\alpha>1\). One-step range membership is exactly \(\{x/\alpha\}>1-1/\alpha\). Applying this again gives \(\{v+(1-u)/\alpha\}>1-1/\alpha\), and its argument lies strictly between zero and two. Splitting at the sole possible carry produces disjoint regions \(C_\alpha\) and \(E_\alpha\). The carry triangle exists exactly when \(1<\alpha<\varphi\) and has area \((1-\alpha+\alpha^{-1})^2/(2\alpha)\). Under rational independence, Kronecker–Weyl equidistribution proves this is its natural density. Strict boundaries, the exact example \(\alpha=\sqrt[3]{3}\), and the exceptional empty-triangle orbit at \(\alpha=\sqrt2\) were addressed. The finite checker is corroboration, not an infinite proof.
